rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine sovereignty is perfectly ordered because God comprehends all; human rulers often lose knowledge of distant parts of their realm, and that ignorance disrupts rule.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الملك لا ينتظم غاية الانتظام إلا بإحاطة العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God already knows what is recited aloud, so reciters need not raise their voices for His sake; loudness is fitting when commanded to make others hear.
rows.anchor: فلا يتكلف ذلك في غير ما أمرت بالجهر به لغرض غير الإسماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secret is what two people whisper privately in fear; the more hidden includes unexpressed thoughts and unseen matters known only to God, including future intentions.
rows.anchor: وهو ما يناجي به الثنان مخافته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's hidden knowledge includes what minds imagine but do not express, other unseen matters no one else knows, and future intentions.
rows.anchor: من ذلك , وهو ما في الضمائر مما تخيلته الأفكار ولم يبرز إلى الخارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Allah opens the declaration as the greatest name, encompassing attributes of majesty and all other divine qualities.
rows.anchor: مفتتحا بالاسم الأعظم الحاوي لصفات الكبر وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that no deity exists but Him rejects any supposed rival to the One whose knowledge and power are complete.
rows.anchor: نفى ذلك بقوله معلما أن هذا ظن باطل قطعا لا شبهة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beautiful names denote perfect attributes that cannot contain deficiency and belong to God truly and continually.
rows.anchor: أي صفات الكمال التي لا يصح ولا يتصور أن يشوبها نقص ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings may possess only some good qualities temporarily and later become unable to sustain them, unlike God's perfect attributes.
rows.anchor: كما يكون لغيره من الاتصاف ببعض المحاسن في بعض الأحايين ثم يعجز عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transition to Moses recalls the question whether anyone is God's namesake or shares His attributes with the same power; the answer is no.
rows.anchor: وأرشد ذلك إلى أن المعنى : هل تعلم له سميا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' story is tangible proof that God's unique beautiful attributes include complete power and exclusive majesty.
rows.anchor: وعطف عليه القصة شاهدا محسوسا على ما له من التصاف بما انتفى عن غيره من الأسماء الحسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story foreshadows God's support for Muhammad through revelation, victory over rulers and adversaries, territorial power, many followers, and honored supporters despite the humble beginning.
rows.anchor: إسعادك في الدارين تكثير أجرك , وتفخيم أمرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign from Pharaoh's Lord is a great proof, including the staff and hand, that obliges him to accept the messengers' claim and submit to guidance.
rows.anchor: موجبة لقبول ما ادعيناه من العصا واليد وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the address intensifies Pharaoh's reproach for claiming lordship and denying God's favor; peace is specifically his if he accepts guidance.
rows.anchor: وفي تكرير مخاطبته بذلك تأكيد لتبكيته في ادعاء الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Peace belongs generally to everyone who follows guidance; refusal leaves Pharaoh exposed to destruction and punishment.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان هذا الجنس عليهم كان من المعلوم أن العطب على غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment covers every denier and one who turns away; the nominal construction presents it as established and enduring.
rows.anchor: لأن اللام للاستغراق أو الماهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning the speech away from Pharaoh signals that he is astray and a denier, and models proper etiquette.
rows.anchor: وفي صرف الكلام عنه تنبيه على أنه ضال مكذب وتعليم للأدب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh chooses debate rather than force so that he will not be accused of foolishness and ignorance.
rows.anchor: أي فرعون مدافعا لهما بالمناظرة لا بالبطش , لئلا ينسب إلى السفه والجهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By asking who their Lord is rather than asking about his own Lord, Pharaoh evades fair consideration and redirects the question to expose them to humiliation.
rows.anchor: حيدة عن سواء النظر وصرفا للكالم على الوجه الموضح لخزيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is singled out because he is the principal in the mission, although Pharaoh had addressed both messengers.
rows.anchor: ولما كان موسى عليه السلام هو الأصل في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses answers immediately that their Lord is their creator, nurturer, and master.
rows.anchor: { ربنا } أي موجدنا ومربينا ومولانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives each existing thing its fitting form and qualities, including shape, size, color, temperament, benefits, and effects.
rows.anchor: أي ما هو عليه مما هو به أليق في المنافع المنوطة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God then guides every animal, rational or not, to its benefits and harms, so it pursues the former and avoids the latter.
rows.anchor: أي كل حيوان منه مع أن فيها العاقل وغيه إلى جميع منافعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word then marks the majesty of imparting spirit, beside which other differences diminish.
rows.anchor: في إفاضة الروح من الجلالة والعظم ما يضمحل عنده غيره من المفاوتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The varied forms and guidance, despite creatures' equal relation to their maker, prove one freely choosing agent; nature governed by stars or other forces could not explain the differences.
rows.anchor: فثبت بهذه المفاوتة والمفاضلة مع اتحاد نسبة الكل إلى الفاعل أنه واحد مختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Moses gives a concise, sound answer, Pharaoh diverts to the former generations, opening a broad, unprovable dispute; the diversion signals that his argument is failing despite his practiced deceit.
rows.anchor: صرف الكلام بسرعة خوف من الاتضاح , بزيادة موسى عليه السلام في الإيضاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses refuses an unproductive argument about the generations; the Torah had not yet been revealed, since it came after Pharaoh's destruction.
rows.anchor: لم تكن التوراة نزلت عليه إذ ذاك , وإنما نزلت بعد هلاك فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generations' knowledge is with God in a book, identified as the Preserved Tablet; God describes it through the familiar human practice of keeping records.
rows.anchor: { في كتاب } أي اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has assigned angels to record His servants' affairs, another familiar reason to speak of a book.
rows.anchor: وكان تعالى قد وكل بعباده من ملائكته من يضبط ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge neither misses any aspect nor forgets any report or other matter.
rows.anchor: ولا نسي وجها يدخل منه شيء من خلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This rebukes Jews: if prophethood required an answer to every question, they would have to doubt their own prophet, who did not explain the generations to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك إشارة إلى تبكيت اليهود بأن ثبوت النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of earth, paths, and rain resumes the rational proof that the creator is one and freely chooses.
rows.anchor: الدليل العقلي على وحدة الصانع واختياره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most of earth is made like a bed, while mountains and contrasting soft and hard regions vary in whether people can settle on them.
rows.anchor: تفترشونها , وجعل بعضها جبالا لا يمكن القرار عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes routes passable across flat and rough terrain and between mountains, valleys, and sands, providing water and pasture; some places remain impassable.
rows.anchor: سهل طرقا تسلكونها في أراضي سهلة وحزنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The differences in terrain and its useful order cannot arise from a uniform natural cause; they show one deliberate agent.
rows.anchor: فلولا أن الفاعل واحد مختار لم يكن هذا التفاوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain descends from the sky, and its color and taste are directly observable signs.
rows.anchor: { وأنزل من السماء ماء } تشاهدونه في اللون والطعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' absorption in divine majesty makes him recognize God as the true speaker; he effaces himself and all created things, and the speech shifts to the majestic first person.
rows.anchor: استغرق صلى الله عليه وسلم في بحار الجلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings forth paired, mutually resembling kinds of plants, with none entirely without a counterpart.
rows.anchor: { به أزواجا } أي أصنافا متشاكلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plant kinds differ greatly in color, size, benefit, nature, and taste.
rows.anchor: أي مختلفة جدا في الألوان والمقادير والمنافع والطبائع والطعوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands to eat and pasture livestock reveal careful provision: human food comes through cultivation, while animals eat surplus plants people cannot consume.
rows.anchor: جعل أرزاق العباد بعملها تنعيما لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world's provisions meet every creature's needs across changing conditions, for their journey to God and presentation before Him; this completeness proves God does not err or forget.
rows.anchor: أبدع هذا العالم شاملا لكل ما يحتاجه من فيه لما خلقهم له من السفر إليه والعرض عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike God, a human maker eventually discovers defects in a product and must repeatedly work to remove them.
rows.anchor: لو عمل شيئا واجتهد كل الاجتهاد في تكميله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are for minds that restrain their owners from wrongdoing; those blind to them have no effective reason, since useless reason is as if absent. The point is emphasized because deniers reject it.
rows.anchor: العقول التي من شأنها أن تنهى صاحبها عن الغي

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir cites a poem that Ibn Ishaq attributes in the Sira to Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl.
rows.anchor: عزاه ابن اسحاق في السيرة لزيد بن عمرو بن نفيل

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hisham instead attributes the cited poem to Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt.
rows.anchor: وابن هشام لأمية بن أبي الصلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem challenges Pharaoh to claim that he made earth without supports, raised the sky without pillars, set its light, brings the sun, and grows crops and grain.
rows.anchor: فقولا له آأنت سويت هذه بلا وتد حتى استقلت كما هيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After showing that Pharaoh denied and refused, God gives a witnessed example that neither his force nor arrogance saved him, while the obedient were rescued.
rows.anchor: أنه لم يغن عن فرعون شيء من قته ولا استكباره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This command to Moses came long after the encounter with the magicians, after many events that brought further great signs.
rows.anchor: هذا الإيحاء بعد ما تقدم من أمر السحرة بمدة مديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to travel by night uses a verb that means night travel.
rows.anchor: أي ليلا , لأن السري سير الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Israelites God's servants honors them; Pharaoh had first refused to release them and had subjected them to punishment.
rows.anchor: بني إسرائيل الذين لفت قلب فرعون حتى أذن في مسيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is directed toward the Sea of Reeds and strikes it with his staff, so the action is called a strike.
rows.anchor: أي اعمل بضرب البحر بعصاك , ولذلك سماه ضربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular word path is generic because each Israelite tribe received its own path through the sea.
rows.anchor: والمراد بها الجنس , فإنه كان لكل سبط طريقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing the path with the verbal noun dry intensifies the description.
rows.anchor: ووصفها بالمصدر مبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses need fear neither the sea catching him nor the enemy or any other danger; the command guarantees rescue and safety.
rows.anchor: أي أن يدركك شيء من طغيان البحر أو بأس العدو أو غير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command displays God's power over a proud adversary and confirms the opening theme of complete power and knowledge, heralding many followers, defeated enemies, and eventual success.
rows.anchor: استلالا شهوديا على ما قرر أول السورة من شمول القدرة وإحاطة العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh pursues the Israelites with numerous, powerful, arrogant troops, although the Israelites are weak and humiliated.
rows.anchor: أوجد التبع والمسير وراء بني إسرائيل على ذلهم وضعفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea overwhelms Pharaoh and his people in an event beyond description, annihilating them from first to last while the oppressed Israelites suffer no injury.
rows.anchor: أمر لا تحتمل العقول وصفه حق وصفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording first says Pharaoh led his people astray, then negates guidance to make clear that he guided neither himself nor anyone among them.
rows.anchor: نفى ضده ليفيده مع كونه أوكد وأوقع في النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction and rescue complete a witnessed proof that God can save the obedient and destroy the disobedient.
rows.anchor: فتم الدليل الشهودي على تمام القدرة على إنجاء الطائع وإهلاك العاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God turns to Israel with reminders of past and coming favors, honoring them in light of their ancestry.
rows.anchor: أقبلنا على بني إسرائيل ممتنين بما مضى وما يأتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rescued Israel by His overwhelming power from an enemy who had regarded them as insignificant.
rows.anchor: بقدرتنا الباهرة { من عدوكم } الذي كنتم أحقر شيء عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promised all Israel to appear in His presence and be honored at places of mercy; the Torah account is also mentioned in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: كما مضى في البقرة عن نص التوراة - للمثول بحضرتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The right side of the mountain is on their right as they travel toward Abraham's homeland, facing the sea and the direction of Mecca and Yemen.
rows.anchor: الذي على أيمانكم في توجهكم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence first names a religious benefit and then worldly provision: the meeting and guidance precede manna and quails that sustain their bodies.
rows.anchor: ولما بدأ بالمنفعة الدينية , ثنى بالمنفعة الدنيوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The manna and quails sustain Israel's bodies after the earlier rescue and promise of guidance.
rows.anchor: بعد إنزال هذا الكتاب في هذه المواعدة لإنعاش أرواحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to eat signals permission, good provision signals abundance, and the phrase what We provided stresses the greatness of the gift.
rows.anchor: ودل على نعمة الإذن فيه بقوله : { كلوا } ودل على سعته بقوله : { من طيبات ما }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel must not hoard manna for the next day except before the Sabbath, act arrogantly, neglect gratitude, or spend provision outside obedience.
rows.anchor: بالادخار إلى غد في غير يوم الجمعة ولا بغير ذلك من البطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The group reading with kasra makes the wrath become due at its proper time, while al-Kisa'i's damma reading conveys a great descent and forceful settling.
rows.anchor: على قراءة الجماعة بالكسر , ونزولا عظيما وبروكا شديدا - على قراءة الكسائي بالضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever incurs God's wrath perishes like someone who has fallen from a height.
rows.anchor: أي كان حاله حال من سقط من علو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's description as all-forgiving means He covers sins by spreading the veil of pardon.
rows.anchor: أي ستار بإسبال ذيل العفو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance means turning away from sins, including idolatry and acts close to it.
rows.anchor: أي رجع عن ذنوبه من الشرك وما يقاربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith means believing everything that must be believed.
rows.anchor: بكل ما يجب الإيمان به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteous deeds confirm the believer's faith.
rows.anchor: به { وعمل صالحا } تصديقا لإيمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then being guided means continuing righteous action with determined care to follow God's commands in the most pleasing way; the intensive verb form signals deliberate effort.
rows.anchor: أي استمر على العمل الصالح متحريا به إيقاعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence with then marks perseverance in upright guidance as an especially elevated rank.
rows.anchor: رتبة الاستمرار على الاستقامة في غاية العلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author conjectures that Moses eagerly set out before God's eventual speaking time, relying on the general appointment rather than waiting for a specific start instruction.
rows.anchor: لاشتياقه إلى ما رأى من التعرف إليه بمقام الجمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author conjectures that Moses arrived ten days before the time God intended to speak, after initially setting a thirty-day expectation for the people.
rows.anchor: فتعجل بعشرة أيام عن الوقت الذي علم الله أ , الكلام يقع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses urged Israel and the seventy selected men to follow him and remain at the places God designated, but they delayed because of the gravity of the scene.
rows.anchor: وتقدم إليهم في اتباعه والطكون في أثره للحلول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author conjectures that after thirty days the delayed meeting was extended ten more; Israel speculated during that interval and adopted the calf.
rows.anchor: فلما مضت الثلاثون بعد ذهاب موسى لم يكن أتى الوقت الذي أراد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later apostasy contrasts with Israel's prior visible and audible signs, showing God's power to turn hearts contrary to expectation.
rows.anchor: أتبع ذلك ذكر ضلالهم بعد رؤية ما يبعد معه كل البعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keeping an appointment delights the heart; the context implies Israel should have gone to the mountain while Moses hurried ahead and they lagged.
rows.anchor: وكان تنجز المواعيد إلذ شيء للقلوب وأشهاه إلى النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks what caused Moses to hurry away from his people; royal boundaries should not be crossed by arriving early or late.
rows.anchor: أن حدود الملوك لا ينبغي تجاوزها بتقدم أو تأخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses should have waited for a new, explicit instruction naming the time at which God summoned them.
rows.anchor: بخصوص الوقت الذي استحضركم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses answers because he assumes his people are following behind him.
rows.anchor: موسى ظنا منه أنهم أسرعوا وراءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative is used without the attention particle because that form is unsuitable when addressing God.
rows.anchor: { هم } وأتى باسم الإشارةواسقط منه هاء التنبيه لأنه لا يليق بخطاب الله

rows.speaker: ابن هبيرة
rows.claim: Ibn Hubayra says he has never seen one of the elect address God with that particle; it was used toward unbelievers because of their dullness.
rows.anchor: قال ابن هبيرة : ولم أر أحدا من الأصفيء خاطب ربه بذلك , وإنما خاطب به الكفار لغباوتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative means the people are near enough to point toward; they walk on Moses' trail before his footprints fade, and he claims he left only the usual short lead among companions.
rows.anchor: أي هم في القرب بحيث يسار إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says the people are walking behind him before his tracks disappear, and he only went ahead by the ordinary distance among companions.
rows.anchor: أي ماشين على آثار مشييي قبل أن ينطمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says he hurried to God seeking greater approval, addressing Him with the familiarity of one who hastens to repair his affairs.
rows.anchor: { وعجلت } أنا بالمبادرة { إليك } وجرى على عادة أهل القرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses addresses God as the one who hastens to set his affairs right.
rows.anchor: أي ايها المسارع في إصلاح شأني والإصلاح إلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says He tested Israel after Moses' departure by a trial that changed their state; the wording indicates the trial occupied only part of the time.
rows.anchor: أي خالطنا بعظمتنا مخالطة مميلة محيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trial took actual effect after the initial thirty-day period and the extra time Moses hurried ahead; his delayed return allowed Israel's temptation to take hold.
rows.anchor: فلما تأخر رجوعك إليهم حصل لهم الفتون بالفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trial affected all but twelve thousand of more than six hundred thousand, yet the whole group is described as astray.
rows.anchor: ولما عمتهم الفتنة إلا اثني عشر ألفا من أكثر من ستمائة ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Samaritan led Israel away from right guidance through what he caused among them.
rows.anchor: أي عن طريق الرشد بما سبب لهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Nasa'i, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim report from Ibn Abbas in the hadith of al-futun that Moses appointed Harun over Israel and set out for a promised meeting of thirty days.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في حديث الفتون أن موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the report, Moses fasted thirty days and nights, then ate a plant because he disliked speaking to God with altered breath; God reminded him a faster's breath is sweeter than musk and ordered ten more days of fasting.
rows.anchor: فصامها ليلها ونهارها , ثم كره أن يكلم ربه وريح فمه متغير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The report says Israel became distressed when Moses did not return, and Harun urged them to account for Egyptian deposits and loans without stealing or keeping them.
rows.anchor: فلما رأى قوم موسى أنه لم يرجع إليهم ساءهم ذلك , كان هارون قد خطبهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Harun dug a pit, had the Israelites place borrowed goods and jewelry in it, and burned them; the excerpt ends as he begins to speak.
rows.anchor: فحفر حفيرا وأمر كل قوم عندهم من ذلك من متاع أو حلية أن يقذفوه في ذلك الحفير
